evidence: Cic. Off. 2.5: nec quicquam aliud est philosophia, sī interpretārī velīs, quam studium sapientiae (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Cicero’s own gloss: the pursuit of wisdom. The philosopher is philosophus; to philosophise, philosophārī.
The Latin for what philosophia seeks; it can stand for philosophy itself, as in Wolff’s sapientia Sīnēnsis (Morgan–Owens).

phrases.latin: ō vītae philosophia dux, ō virtūtis indāgātrīx expultrīxque vitiōrum!
phrases.english: O philosophy, guide of life, tracker of virtue and banisher of vices!

phrases.latin: quae philosophia fuit facta philologia est
phrases.english: what was philosophy has become philology

sources: Lewis & Short: philosophia · Lewis & Short: sapientia
